findings.quote: `require-org.ts`: `requireOrgMember(slug)` → … (a super admin with `membership_status = null` passes — step 3.1 may narrow this; keep the rule in one function)
findings.problem: Contradicts the rest of G5 and G7: 2.2b's Finish adds a founder to-do 'create or invite yourself as first admin so `/o/<slug>` opens for you (super admins are not org members)', proposed step 3.11 exists precisely because `requireOrgMember` 404s for super admins, and G7's 3.1 prompt states 'Super admins who are not members also get 404 here'. DESIGN §5/§9 define `requireOrgMember` on `org_memberships` only. As written, 2.1 builds the opposite behaviour and the founder to-do / 3.11 become wrong.
findings.fix: Replace the parenthesis with: '(a super admin without an `active` membership also gets `notFound()` — super admins are `super_admins` rows, not org members (DESIGN §5); leave a code comment pointing at proposed step 3.11, which lifts this)'. Update the 2.1 done_when/notes accordingly; keep 2.2b's founder to-do and 3.11 as they are.

findings.quote: Add `src/lib/supabase/errors.ts`: `toActionError(err)` that maps a PostgREST/RPC error to `{key, message}` using `@church/domain` `errors.ts` (match `message` against the catalogue keys; fall back to a generic message…)
findings.problem: G4 (1.6b/1.7b) already ships this layer: `@church/domain` exports `DomainError` and `toDomainError` (SQLSTATE + snake_case message-key convention, `23514` → `invalid_payload`), and `@church/db` wraps every query/RPC in `unwrap`/`unwrapVoid`/`unwrapStorage` so 'callers never see raw Supabase errors'. 2.1 re-implements the matching in the app under a new name, and 2.2a/2.2b then call `toActionError` five times — two parallel error mappers with different rules.
findings.fix: Rewrite the bullet: '`src/lib/supabase/errors.ts`: `toActionError(err: unknown): ActionError` is a thin adapter — if `err instanceof DomainError` (from `@church/domain`) return `{key: err.key, message: err.message}`, else call `toDomainError(err)` first; never match strings in the app. All DB access goes through the `@church/db` wrappers, which already return `DomainError`.' Update Inputs bullet 3 to name `toDomainError`/`DomainError`/`ERROR_MESSAGES` (G4's names) instead of 'error key → message map'.

findings.quote: Always render an **"Open in app"** button linking to `anacast://invite/<token>`
findings.problem: G4's 1.6b exports `inviteDeepLink(token)` in `@church/domain` `urls.ts` (unit-tested to return `anacast://invite/abc`) and `shareLinkUrl`. Hand-building the scheme URL in the page duplicates the single source of the `anacast` scheme (orchestrator decision 5).
findings.fix: Change to: 'linking to `inviteDeepLink(token)` from `@church/domain` (`urls.ts`, step 1.6b) — do not hard-code the scheme; `APP_SCHEME` in `src/lib/brand.ts` must equal the value `urls.ts` uses'.

findings.quote: …`frame-ancestors 'none'`. Add `X-Frame-Options: DENY` on a second `headers()` entry whose `source` matches everything EXCEPT `/s/:path*` and `/embed/:path*` … for `/embed/*` also omit `frame-ancestors 'none'`
findings.problem: The CSP (including `frame-ancestors 'none'`) is attached to the `/(.*)` entry, so it also lands on `/s/*` and `/embed/*`; a second `headers()` entry cannot 'omit' a directive from the first, and browsers honour CSP `frame-ancestors` over `X-Frame-Options`. DESIGN §9 wants `/s/*` and `/embed/*` frame-able (the `/embed/yt/[id]` page is the mobile WebView host and must not be locked to `'none'`).
findings.fix: Use the same negative-lookahead source for the CSP entry as for `X-Frame-Options` (both on `/((?!s/|embed/).*)`), and give `buildCsp({ frameable: boolean })` in `src/lib/security/csp.ts` the option to emit `frame-ancestors *` (or omit it) so step 3.4 sets the exempt routes' CSP itself. Adjust the csp.test.ts bullet to assert `frame-ancestors 'none'` only for the default variant.

findings.problem: G4 split the steps into 1.6a/1.6b and 1.7a/1.7b (and G2/G3 into 1.3a/1.3b, 1.4a/1.4b/1.4c); the prompt already says '1.3b/1.4' in one place but '1.7' elsewhere, and `depends_on` names a step id that will not exist in the assembled TODO.

findings.quote: if there is no schema for creating a church or for the full settings row, add `organizationCreateSchema`, `organizationUpdateSchema` and `organizationSettingsSchema` to `packages/domain/src/schemas/org.ts` / `schemas/settings.ts`
findings.problem: G4's 1.6b already defines these under different names: `createOrganizationSchema` (defaults `trial_ends_at` to now + 30 days per founder decision 7), `updateOrganizationSchema` (partial + `status`), `fellowshipSchema` (`slug`, `name`, `description`), `orgBillingFormSchema`, `organizationSettingsSchema`, `updateSettingsSchema` + `validateSettingsUpdate(current, patch)`, `timezoneSchema`, `DEFAULT_SETTINGS`. The 2.2a agent following this text would add duplicates `organizationCreateSchema`/`organizationUpdateSchema`, and `src/features/orgs/trial.ts` re-implements the 30-day default the schema already has.
findings.fix: Replace with: 'Use `createOrganizationSchema`, `updateOrganizationSchema`, `organizationSettingsSchema`, `updateSettingsSchema`/`validateSettingsUpdate`, `fellowshipSchema`, `timezoneSchema` and `DEFAULT_SETTINGS` from `@church/domain` (step 1.6b); if a name differs, adopt the exported one and record it in HANDOFF — do not add parallel schemas.' Rename every later mention (`organizationCreateSchema` in Build 2, `organizationUpdateSchema` in Build 4). Make `src/features/orgs/trial.ts` a re-export/wrapper of the schema default, and have `fields.test.ts` compare against `DEFAULT_SETTINGS` keys.

findings.quote: "New fellowship" dialog with Name → Server Action `createFellowship`), `app/(super)/admin/fellowships/[id]/page.tsx` (rename form → `renameFellowship`
findings.problem: DESIGN §4.2: `fellowships` = `id, slug citext unique, name, description`. A Name-only dialog cannot satisfy the unique slug column, and the rename form ignores `slug`/`description`. G4's `fellowshipSchema` already has `slug`, `name`, `description`.
findings.fix: Build 7: 'New fellowship dialog: Name, Slug (auto-derived with `slugify`, editable, unique — map `23505` to a slug field error), Description (optional); validate with `fellowshipSchema`. The `[id]` page edits Name, Slug (with the same URL-change warning as churches) and Description via `updateFellowship`.' Add `slug` to the Inputs description of `fellowships`.

findings.quote: Server Action `saveOrgSettings(orgId, values)`: `requireSuperAdmin()`, Zod parse, `update organization_settings … where org_id = orgId` with the user client
findings.problem: DESIGN §5 'Suspended orgs': `app.org_writable` is required by every write policy; G3's `organization_settings` update policy is `org.settings` ∧ writable. For a `suspended` or `cancelled` church the super admin's update matches zero rows and PostgREST returns success — the form would toast 'saved' while nothing changed. Founder decision 7 makes suspension the one state that blocks writes, so the UI must reflect it.
findings.fix: Add to Build 5: 'When `organizations.status` is `suspended` or `cancelled`, render the Settings form read-only with the note "This church is suspended — writes are blocked by the database (founder decision 7). Unsuspend it on the Billing tab (2.2b) first." In `saveOrgSettings` request the updated row back (`.select().single()`) and treat zero rows as `organization_suspended`.' Apply the same guard to the Details tab's `updateChurch` only if 1.4a's `ca_organizations_update_super` includes `org_writable` (read the policy).

findings.quote: RHF + `zodResolver(inviteAdminSchema)` … USER client → `create_invitation(orgId, email, null, perms)` … `set_membership_permissions(membershipId, PERMISSION_KEYS)` … `revoke_invitation(id)`
findings.problem: `inviteAdminSchema` is invented; G4's 1.6b exports `createInvitationSchema` (parses to `{org, email (lower-cased), person_id: null, perms: []}`) and `createUserDirectSchema` (the latter G5 uses correctly). G4's 1.7b `rpc.ts` wrappers take the client plus an object whose keys are EXACTLY the SQL parameter names (`createInvitation(db, {org, email, person_id, perms})`, `setMembershipPermissions(db, {membership_id, perms})`, `setMembershipStatus(db, {id, status})`, `revokeInvitation(db, {id})`) and parse jsonb results with domain schemas (`attachUserResultSchema` for `srv_attach_user` → `{membership_id, person_id, household_id}`). Positional calls and a second invitation schema diverge from the shared layer.
findings.fix: Replace `inviteAdminSchema` with `createInvitationSchema` (drop the 'add if missing' clause for it). Rewrite every RPC mention as the `@church/db` wrapper with named arguments, e.g. '`createInvitation(db, { org: orgId, email, person_id: null, perms })` (wrapper for `create_invitation`)', '`setMembershipPermissions(db, { membership_id, perms: PERMISSION_KEYS })`', '`revokeInvitation(db, { id })`', '`srvAttachUser(serviceDb, { user_id, org, person_id, display_name, perms })` whose result is `attachUserResultSchema`'. Update done_when bullet 2 to the named-argument form.

findings.problem: Same as the 2.1 finding: `toActionError` must be the thin adapter over `@church/domain` `DomainError`/`toDomainError`, not a second string-matching mapper. 2.2b also maps the Supabase Auth error `email_exists` — that is an Auth (GoTrue) error code, not a DB catalogue key, so it must be handled before/outside the DB mapper.
findings.fix: State in Build 2 step 3: 'Auth errors come from `auth.admin.createUser` (`error.code === "email_exists"` or status 422) and are mapped in `create-direct.ts` itself; DB/RPC errors are `DomainError`s from the `@church/db` wrappers and pass through `toActionError`.'
